resources.exclusion_reason: DEPLOYED host device but outside the InferSwarm execution fleet boundary: it is the PCIe-topology test host's display/general GPU. It is classified here per the correction directive (no silent omission), counted in the physical-fleet aggregate, and excluded from every InferSwarm runtime-fit subset. Its 3 GiB would not fit any plausible R8 weight shard regardless.

Maintainer relayed a 3x RX 580 inventory; only two Ellesmere devices are observable on any reachable deployed host (inferswarm02 02:00.0 and 03:00.0). A sweep of every reachable host (inferswarm00-04, valinor, buildbox, monomyth-build, pm01, pm04, readynas, plex, rproxy; receipts retained) found no third Polaris and no Navi device. Offline hosts cannot be excluded, but no reachable deployed host exposes it; it is not current execution authority and contributes zero bytes to deployed totals.

r8_runtime_mode_subset.proposed_mode: llama.cpp, heterogeneous CUDA(+Vulkan optional) layer-split cross-host RPC, Unsloth UD-IQ1_S, n-gram/PLE table host-resident
r8_runtime_mode_subset.weight_resident_subset_rationale: For the proposed R8 mode the whole 96-GiB NVIDIA execution pool (80 GiB on 01-04 + 16 GiB AMD if a Vulkan arm is included) is CANDIDATE capacity; exact per-resource fit is NOT_ESTABLISHED. The retained R8-A conclusions make no per-resource allocation claim beyond the representation-level facts in gguf-header-census.json (backbone minus PLE table ~40.74 GiB; PLE table 26.82 GiB; neither implies residency feasibility).

non_claims: No GPU was initialized, no CUDA/Vulkan context was created, and no model or benchmark was executed.
nvidia-smi --query-gpu is a driver query, not correctness-bearing GPU work.
Aggregate VRAM is not a feasibility proof; per-resource fit constraints for R8 are NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Backend capability is not Qwen3.8 qualification: accepted Vulkan work proves llama.cpp Vulkan on specific devices for Qwen2.5-3B Q4_K_M only.
x1 riser topology limits communication-sensitive utility, not capacity utility; no throughput claim is made in either direction.
Offline-host devices cannot be mechanically excluded; the reported-not-observed rows document exactly what was and was not seen, on which hosts, when.
The V340L is pending hardware: zero bytes, zero authority, not current capacity.
